terms.gloss: put first, count as more important
terms.grammar: phrase: neuter comparative of antīquus, with habēre or with esse and the dative (mihi antīquius est)
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.3: quod honestius, id mihi est antīquius (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 11.5: neque habuī quicquam antīquius quam ut … (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: in the comparative and superlative antīquus means “before or first in rank or importance”. Nihil antīquius habeō quam ut …: my first priority is to …. The adjective’s plain sense is “old, of former times”.

terms.gloss: first of all, before everything else
evidence: Quint. 1.1.4: ante omnia nē sit vitiōsus sermō nūtrīcibus
Liv. 8.29.2: nūlla prior potiorque vīsa est (Lewis & Short s.v. prior)

phrases.latin: quod honestius, id mihi est antīquius
phrases.english: whatever is more honourable comes first for me

phrases.latin: ante omnia nē sit vitiōsus sermō nūtrīcibus
phrases.english: first of all, let the nurses’ speech be free of faults

phrases.latin: Nihil mihi antīquius est quam ut valeās.
phrases.english: Nothing matters more to me than your health.
